question: Does the compile-time UDOT dot-product kernel speed up the stable core's fixed-scale match, with bit-identical outputs?
toolchain: Apple clang 21.0.0, CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release, FPM_WITH_OPENCV=ON, default target-cpu apple-m1 for both builds
benchmark_modes: cpp-core/tools/benchmark_modes.py --repeats 9 (one warm-up + 9 measured per mode, fresh process each); sessions interleaved before,after,before,after,before,after; the before sessions run the frozen base copy of the script so source hashes describe the base source
control: legacy_cpp mode is the same macos-cli/match_core.cpp source in both builds; its medians track environment drift
fixture_ab: cpp-core/tools/benchmark_backend_ab.py --rounds 8 (round 0 warm-up discarded), order alternates per round, 17 compare_versions cases
metric: fpm_cli match_ms (excludes image decoding and learning); medians per session; no runs dropped or rerun
acceptance: speed is reported, not gated; identity is gated separately by check_backend_identity.py and compare_versions.py
environment_note: other Claude sessions may be active on this machine; load averages are recorded per session
